title: Neural Networks Basics: Perceptron to Dropout
summary: Quick revision notes on neural network fundamentals: the perceptron, layers and activations, forward and backward passes, loss and optimizers, training loops, and dropout regularization.

chapters.title: Perceptron and Layers: The Mental Model
points: Perceptron: output = activation(w·x + b); weights scale inputs, bias shifts the decision threshold
A single perceptron draws one linear boundary, so it cannot solve XOR
A layer is many neurons sharing the same input: y = f(W x + b), with W shaped (out, in)
Stacking layers only helps if each has a nonlinear activation; without it, N linear layers collapse into one linear map
Parameters in a dense layer = in × out + out (weights plus biases)

chapters.title: Activations: ReLU, Sigmoid, Softmax
points: ReLU: max(0, x); cheap, default for hidden layers, but neurons stuck at negative input get zero gradient (dying ReLU)
Sigmoid: 1/(1+e^-x) maps to (0,1); use for binary output; saturates at the extremes so gradients vanish
Softmax: e^xi / Σ e^xj turns logits into probabilities summing to 1; use for multi-class output
Match output to task: sigmoid + binary cross-entropy, softmax + categorical cross-entropy, none for regression
Subtract max(x) before exponentiating in softmax to avoid overflow

chapters.title: Forward Pass and Backpropagation
points: Forward pass: feed input layer by layer, a = f(W a_prev + b), and cache each layer's inputs and pre-activations for the backward pass
Backprop applies the chain rule from loss back to each weight: dL/dW = dL/da · da/dz · dz/dW
Layer gradients: dW = δ · a_prevᵀ, db = δ, and the error passed back is δ_prev = Wᵀ δ ⊙ f'(z)
Vanishing gradients come from repeated multiplication by values below 1 (sigmoid derivative max is 0.25); ReLU eases this
Training step order: forward, loss, zero gradients, backward, optimizer step
Forgetting to zero gradients makes them accumulate across batches (PyTorch)

chapters.title: Loss Functions and Optimizers: SGD vs Adam
points: MSE for regression; cross-entropy −Σ y log(ŷ) for classification
Gradient descent update: w ← w − lr · ∂L/∂w
SGD with momentum keeps a velocity of past gradients, which smooths noisy steps and speeds convergence
Adam tracks a running mean (m) and variance (v) of gradients with per-parameter step sizes; defaults lr=1e-3, β1=0.9, β2=0.999
SGD often generalizes better and needs tuned lr and schedule; Adam converges fast with little tuning
Learning rate too high diverges or oscillates; too low crawls; it is the first hyperparameter to tune

chapters.title: Epochs, Batches and Dropout
points: Epoch = one full pass over the training set; iteration = one batch update; iterations per epoch = N / batch_size
Mini-batch is the usual compromise: full-batch is stable but slow and memory heavy, batch size 1 is noisy
Shuffle training data every epoch; never shuffle or augment the validation set
Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction p of activations during training and rescales by 1/(1−p), acting as a regularizer
Call model.eval() at inference to disable dropout; forgetting this gives noisy predictions
Typical p: 0.2–0.5 for dense layers; use early stopping when validation loss rises while training loss falls

chapters.title: Neural Network Cheat Sheet
points: Hidden layers: ReLU; binary output: sigmoid; multi-class output: softmax; regression: linear
Loss pairing: MSE for regression, binary cross-entropy for sigmoid, categorical cross-entropy for softmax
Training loop: forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step
Starting points: Adam lr=1e-3, batch size 32–128, dropout 0.2–0.5
Debug checklist: overfit one small batch first; loss NaN means lr too high or bad softmax/log; train/val gap means more regularization
